program: Sexual and reproductive health funding, clinical support, research and advocacy

what: Essential Access Health supports sexual and reproductive health services, training and public-program administration.
Its California partner-treatment program supplies medication for eligible partners unlikely to obtain timely clinical care.
The conditional estimate prices only repeat-infection prevention against all recipient costs; the larger reproductive-health portfolio remains unpriced.
strengths: Partner STI treatment has randomized evidence of reducing persistent or recurrent infections.
The organization operates a concrete medication distribution pathway with site logs and expired-dose reporting.
Current public funding announcements and original returns allow scrutiny of pass-through funding and substitution.
reservations: No verified ordinary-gift allocation, incremental medication yield or currently unfunded treatment queue was found.
Large restricted public grants and reimbursements are not equivalent to private-donation-sensitive additional care.
Sex, pathogen, treatment timing and recurrent-infection risks materially change the QALY conversion.

sections.what:
This is the entire Essential Access Health recipient, EIN 95-2564024, rather than a restricted medication project. Its activities include provider funding, training, clinical research and policy. The official site links the ordinary donation route, but no gift or endorsement was made. [Current programs and ordinary donation link](https://www.essentialaccess.org/programs-and-services)

One inspectable clinical pathway is California expedited partner therapy: eligible providers obtain free medication for partners unlikely to receive prompt treatment. This is a delivery mechanism, not evidence that every distributed dose is taken or prevents infection. [California free partner-treatment program](https://orders.essentialaccess.org/about)
sections.monitoring:
The medication system requires site-specific logs and reporting of expired stock, with a licensed repackager shipping on the organization's request. The index patient's own treatment matters because a partner pack can otherwise be diverted to that patient. Useful marginal monitoring would add unique index patients offered treatment, partner uptake, alternative access, repeat infection and the funding source of each additional offer. [Partner medication distribution and accountability FAQ](https://orders.essentialaccess.org/faq)

In a 2005 randomized trial, persistent or recurrent infection at 3–19 weeks occurred in 121/931 standard-referral patients versus 92/929 expedited-treatment patients: relative risk 0.76 (95% CI 0.59–0.98). Effects differed by pathogen; the composite absolute reduction cannot simply be paired with the highest sex-specific disease burden. [Randomized expedited partner treatment trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15716561/)

A later Washington stepped-wedge community trial increased EPT receipt but its adjusted population outcomes were uncertain: chlamydia positivity prevalence ratio 0.89 (0.77–1.04) and gonorrhea incidence ratio 0.91 (0.71–1.16). Clinic efficacy therefore does not establish the population return on a statewide implementation dollar. [Washington community randomized EPT implementation trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25590331/)
sections.qualitative:
Access, privacy and reproductive autonomy can matter independently of measured health. This report does not convert avoided births or the monetary value of care into QALYs. Training attendance, grant awards and reimbursed visits likewise are not themselves health outcomes.

EPT supplements rather than universally replaces clinical evaluation. Current CDC guidance describes its role when partners are unlikely to access timely care; trial transfer must respect current eligibility and treatment practice. [Current clinical treatment of gonorrhea](https://www.cdc.gov/gonorrhea/hcp/clinical-care/index.html)

The strongest next diligence request is a costed, currently unfunded California delivery margin: how many additional eligible patients would receive and use partner treatment, compared with Medi-Cal, Family PACT, ordinary partner referral and other free sources? Existing payment alternatives are explicitly described on the patient page. [Partner medication and existing payment options](https://www.essentialaccess.org/partner_meds)

EPT can change actual partner payments or time spent obtaining care, but free alternative supply and an otherwise missed visit make retail savings inappropriate. All genuinely incremental delivery burdens persist independently of clinical success; only net positive resources receive overlap discount.
sections.cost:
Current conditional signed reference: $803.22 million per ten equivalent healthy years, combining unchanged0.858685California clinicalQALYs and−0.277577household-resource equivalents at$46,675,922annual full recipient cost. Resource equivalents compare welfare, not measured clinicalQALYs. Original health-only$543.57million and every original world remain diagnostics.

The following original clinical calculation remains the health-only diagnostic, not the current signed headline.

The conditional EPT repeat-infection prevention price is $543.57 million per ten California QALYs, charging all $46,675,922 of gross recognized recipient spending. This narrow component must not be presented as a complete reproductive-health return. A 5% EPT allocation and $100 full delivery-resource cost per eligible index-patient offer are judgments, not observed marginal program costs or medication quotes. The resource allowance includes drug, logistics, counseling and partner delivery; an additional partner-resource sensitivity is retained.

The trial's absolute repeat-infection difference is 121/931 minus 92/929, about 3.094 percentage points among followed participants. A 50% transfer factor discounts current patient mix, follow-up selection, treatment practice and the uncertain community implementation evidence. A separate 25% funding-response factor discounts payer replacement and existing free supply. We use a judgmental 0.01 discounted QALY per repeat infection avoided, not the largest female infection burden paired indiscriminately with a pooled effect. A 98% California resident share gives 0.858685 California QALYs.

No partner or downstream transmission benefit is added, no new lifetime is assigned to recurrences, and no extra adherence factor duplicates the trial strategy effect. The underlying disease model uses finite sequela duration; an additional 3% one-year timing discount only moves the avoided infection to the delivery date. Routine medication harms and missed clinical evaluations could offset benefits; zero and adverse stress cases remain.

Fresh original program information describes free medication for partners unlikely to obtain timely care, delivered through clinics/LHJs or index patients without another partner examination. Patient information describes existing Medi-Cal/FamilyPACT low-cost/free alternatives. No observed private-payment saving or incremental household cost is reported. [Program](https://orders.essentialaccess.org/about) [Existing payment alternatives](https://www.essentialaccess.org/partner_meds)

The annual resource participation hypothesis is23,337.961offer-equivalents times25%fundingresponse times98%California share, or5,717.800445partner-household-equivalent offers. One unique participating partner household per offer is a distribution judgment, not a medication-log count; a half-participation world tests duplicates/nonparticipation. Clinical trial effect, transfer and infectionresponse do not reduce incurred resource burdens. Existing index diagnostic visit is baseline: do not add its full attendance cost to a marginal EPTpack.

The $2burden is hypothesized incremental unreimbursed household disposable-resource/opportunity loss NOT represented in recipient gross spending or k provider/drug/logistics allowance. If it overlaps those resources, net it out: the financial-null world sets burden0 and cash0. Added real-resource stress excludes this same household loss, and payer-consumption loss is disjoint, not duplicate financing. Central assumes zero actual private spending saving and a hypothetical full$2incremental handling/delivery/time opportunity burden for every participated offer-equivalent, whether infection is avoided or not, at$20,000annual household resources. One end-of-year resource change uses0.5times5,717.800445divided by1.03times log(1−2/20000). Dollars and household count are illustrative judgments, not measured client charges or income.

A conditional private-saving world assigns$50actual displaced private payment/time cost to20%of households, retains80%after taxes, benefit withdrawal and substitution, discounts only positive gains50%for health overlap, and subtracts FULL$2burden from both saver/non-saver groups before separate joint logs. No retail medication/medical value, public grant, ordinary survivor wages or gross job salary is income. Financial-only/clinical-null, unknown/null, noresponse, adversecost and zero-positive-overlap worlds remain explicit. Public free supply/payer replacement already enters fundingresponse once;100,000gift scales cost/reach consistently, not verified restricted capacity. Disjoint public consumption loss and added real delivery resources are separate stress scopes, never duplicate a transfer. Broader familyplanning, TitleX, research, professional capacity, autonomy and policy income/consumption effects remainunknown, not zero.
sections.funding:
Original accrual returns and Schedule D yield gross expenses of $31,893,649 in 2022, $52,995,581 in 2023 and $46,675,922 in 2024, averaging $43,855,050.67. The earlier comparative comes from the 2023 return. [Original 2023 Form 990 with 2022 comparative totals](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/952564024/202403209349311455/full)

In 2024, $40,147,199 was classified as program expense and $6,525,628 as administration. Revenue was $37,119,151, including $32,635,022 government grants. Despite the revenue-expense deficit, unrestricted net assets rose from $7,995,747 to $8,641,940 while restricted net assets fell from $15,543,653 to $5,998,097. This is consistent with restricted-fund spending timing and does not establish an unrestricted cash crisis. Neither balances nor functional ratios identify marginal cost-effectiveness. [Original 2024 Form 990](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/952564024/202543179349311349/full)

April 2026's announcement says California and Hawaii Title X received one year of level funding; describing the prior withholding as still unresolved would be stale. [2026 Title X award received](https://www.essentialaccess.org/about/press-room/essential-access-health-receives-title-x-funding-amid-ongoing-federal-uncertainty)

June 2025's final-award announcement described $36.5 million cumulatively awarded for uncompensated care, including reimbursement of earlier services. Those patients cannot all be attributed to a new gift. [June 2025 uncompensated-care awards](https://www.essentialaccess.org/about/press-room/essential-access-health-announces-final-awards-californias-uncompensated-care)

Current HCAI information now describes a new $30 million uncompensated-care allocation within broader 2026–27 reproductive-health appropriations, with administrator procurement expected in September 2026. Essential Access administered prior funds, but the new award is not yet established as its revenue. State appropriations do not prove all needs are met; they do require avoiding duplicate private-donor credit. [Current reproductive-health appropriations and administrator procurement](https://hcai.ca.gov/workforce/initiatives/reproductive-health-and-gender-affirming-care-programs/)

Fresh original three-year reconciliations restore inventory costs of $17,637, $2,695 and $1,635, plus $1,460 of donated services in 2024. Investment expenses of $57,667, $45,699 and $40,332 already included in return expense are retained, not added twice. No separately netted event cost is reported.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient gross recognized costs. Only EPT repeat-infection health priced, not complete portfolio. k includes modeled delivery resources; partner-resource stress tests additional unrecognized costs. Household burden is incremental unreimbursed disposable-resource/opportunity loss disjoint from recipient gross expense and provider/drug/logistics yield allowance k. External-resource stress excludes the same household loss; disjoint payer consumption is not a duplicated transfer.
model.geographicAttribution: California delivery sites verified, but beneficiaries may include nonresidents: g_CA=.98 subjective, low .9/high1. Not the California share of all Title X or other operations.
model.formula: N=C*f/k; infections_all=N*b*delta*t; Q_all=infections_all*v/(1+d); Q_CA=Q_all*g_CA. delta=121/931-92/929. v is already discounted finite QALY loss per avoided infection; d only one-year event timing. P10=10*C/Q_CA. No secondary transmission or repeated lifetime branches. Resource household-equivalents=N*b*g*participation, no clinical t/delta/v discount on access costs. Joint saver/non-saver netresources afterretention and positive-overlap minus FULLburden; .5*people/(1+d)*log1p(net/baseline). One year, not repeated sequela years or lifetime wages.
model.counterfactual: Existing public funding and free EPT distribution, ordinary partner referral, Medi-Cal/Family PACT and timely alternative care continue. b discounts donation-dependent delivery beyond them. Current level Title X award is baseline, not an unresolved withholding.
model.attribution: Trial strategy effect includes imperfect partner delivery; no second completion/adherence discount. t is external-to-current population/implementation transfer, b funding response. No partner infection health counted separately.
model.uncertainty: Allocation, marginal unit resources, patient mix and donation response remain subjective. The community trial has uncertain population effects. Finite clinical conversion is transferred conservatively but not identified for repeat infections in this population. Unique partner-household-equivalence and participation, actual private spending/time displacement, incremental delivery burden and resource baseline are judgments. Other reproductive-health/autonomy/workforce resource effects remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Central 23337.961 eligible index-patient offer-equivalents before funding response; 90.2495294937617 repeat infections avoided before geography. Modeled quantities, not medication-log counts.
